Main claims are explicit and supported: significant U5MR reduction; IMR effect reported as imprecise. Robustness across models/weighting; attrition balanced. Mechanism claims framed as suggestive; limitations acknowledged (timing mismatch, bad-control concerns). Dose–response evidence strengthens story.

Strong randomized phase-in design; appropriate clustering, covariate adjustment, birth-year FE, weighting; sensitivity checks (logit/probit, alternative weights). Heterogeneity and assigned-years dose–response informative. Weaknesses: self-reported mortality; no formal multiple-testing control; mediation not causal; potential cross-household spillovers/spousal treatment; external validity limits.

Rare causal evidence on intergenerational child survival from adolescent deworming. Extends KLPS literature to mortality outcomes; quantifies channels and cost–benefit. High relevance for debates on deworming’s long-run and intergenerational impacts; informs global health prioritization.

Clear articulation of questions, design, and findings; figures/tables aligned with narrative; assumptions and caveats explicit. Mechanisms section carefully framed. Some complexity (weights, DALY valuation) could be distilled further, but overall reasoning is transparent and consistent.

Trial registered (AEARCTR-0001191), disclosures, detailed appendices, construction notes, and robustness provided. KLPS microdata likely restricted; code availability unclear; stated-preference survey not obviously archived. Replication feasible but nontrivial without full data/code release.

Directly informs child mortality policy in LMICs with high helminth burden; intergenerational benefits matter for cost-effectiveness and prioritization. Communicates actionable magnitudes (per 1000 births; IRRs). High external policy salience despite local sample constraints.

High-impact Nature paper delivering first pantropical 30 m map of natural regeneration potential (≈215 Mha; 23.4 Gt C over 30 years). Strong empirical basis, careful caveats, and policy relevance. Limitations: deterministic mapping with very tight area CI, partial handling of spatial autocorrelation, and code only “on request,” not fully open.

Main claims (extent and distribution of regeneration potential; carbon implications) are clear and largely supported by RF models trained on observed regrowth and validated (~87.9% accuracy). Sensibly interprets drivers (distance to forest, forest density). Caveats noted: humid-biome omission issues, mixed-resolution predictors, stationarity to 2030, and narrow area CI lacking model uncertainty.

Reasonable, well-justified RF with variable selection; extensive covariates; validation includes distance-to-training assessment for autocorrelation. Chose biophysical-only predictors after comparison. Gaps: no full spatial/block cross-validation, limited uncertainty propagation for maps/areas, deterministic carbon aggregation, and potential sampling/label biases from source regrowth product.

Provides first high-resolution, empirically grounded pantropical probability surface for natural regeneration and derived carbon potential, improving on coarse/assumption-driven opportunity maps. Creates actionable inputs for targeting restoration, incentives, and planning; highlights country-level concentration. Likely to be widely used and built upon.

Questions, assumptions, and limitations are explicit; reasoning is transparent; figures/tables are interpretable; partial dependence and accuracy diagnostics aid understanding. Appropriate caution about feasibility, leakage, additionality, permanence, and equity. Minor complexity from mixed-resolution inputs is clearly flagged.

Key 30 m tiles (continuous and binary) released on Zenodo; inputs mostly public; thorough data sourcing. However, analysis code is ‘available on request’ rather than openly archived; not an end-to-end reproducible pipeline; some inputs updated/reprocessed across versions, hindering exact replication.

Directly relevant to nature-based climate solutions, cost-effective restoration, and biodiversity co-benefits. Quantifies large potential (215 Mha; 23.4 Gt C), identifies priority countries, and discusses policy instruments, markets, and equity. Highly actionable for national targets, PES design, and carbon accounting.
